# Jake <> Brent weekly 1:1 (Friday)

## Summary
The discussion reviewed pipeline data quality, performance, ICP priorities, and follow-up actions. Attribution was mostly accurate, but one Salesforce opportunity was wrongly assigned to Jake, Funding Pips required correction as a Dubai-based education company with 1,409 employees, and incomplete records affected opportunity and website-traffic analysis. Performance showed one win and 23 losses among 24 opportunities with outcomes, while low-fit SMB and mid-market opportunities remained a conversion problem. The recommended ICP was B2B technology or software companies with 1,000–10,000 employees, supported by website traffic, Rio signals, Pro usage, and relevant OSS activity. Accounts under 100 employees would require stronger signals, with Pro prioritized over OSS. Brent would clean the data and share findings with Ryan, while Jake would analyze high-Rio, Pro, and OSS accounts. February 1 marked Jake’s one-year point, with approximately $500,000 sourced viewed as a strong first-year outcome. Dripify sequences were deferred to the next meeting.

## Summary
The team reviewed multi-touch campaigns covering approximately 600 contacts across Dripify and Apollo. Phone outreach generated about one-third of meetings, while LinkedIn produced most of the remainder; email supported visibility and name recognition. Messaging was updated with stronger AI positioning, and personalized opening lines were being tested. Reporting should combine Dripify and Apollo data and compare meetings and pipeline conversion by account quality, persona, seniority, traffic, and intent signals. A refined campaign will run alongside existing campaigns for at least one additional week, with separate naming and a benchmark campaign preserved. Airscale and Claude industry estimates will help address unreliable employee, traffic, and industry data. The next goals are to build approximately 200 optimized accounts, launch multi-persona sequences, review results weekly, and pursue one legitimate sub-$100K opportunity.

# Jake <> Brent weekly 1:1 (Friday)
Date: 2026-10-27 | Duration: 35.97999954223633m

## Summary
The team reviewed pipeline generation, campaign performance, and enterprise expansion. Jake prioritized approximately 90 conference leads, about 40 closed-lost accounts, and opportunities from Lamb Research and Daikin, while one podcast-generated meeting had also entered the pipeline. Three prospect sequences targeting CTOs, engineering leaders, and platform or development contacts produced no opportunities yet; LinkedIn generated 11 acceptances from 65 attempts, with three replies. Outreach for the November 5 dinner was prioritized across 472 contacts, while the other sequences were paused and LinkedIn registration-link messaging will be A/B tested. Enterprise targeting shifted from 1–100 to 1,000–10,000 employees, and a HubSpot search identified 144 Pro customers with 50–100 employees, narrowed to 38 companies with more than five licensed seats. Pricing remains a risk because the move from approximately $80 monthly to $50,000 annually may hinder conversion. Unreliable employee data, blocked HubSpot exports, and enrichment needs were also discussed. Jake is expected to spend 10–15% of his time on expansion while maintaining pipeline work, with a goal of finding one interested 100-employee Pro customer.
